data.long_meaning: A name derived from the Arabic root 'f-y-d' meaning 'to be useful, to be beneficial'. In Islamic history, the name Fayid has been given to individuals who have brought about significant change and have been of great benefit to their communities. The name Fayid carries the meaning “Useful, Beneficial” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persianian. Parents who choose Fayid usually hope their child will grow to embody useful, beneficial and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: Fayid ibn al-Jarrah was a prominent early Muslim convert and the first Muslim governor of Damascus. He played a crucial role in the early Islamic conquests and was the first Muslim to rule Damascus, a major city in the Levant.

historical_references.reference: Al-Fayid ibn Ali, a renowned scholar and a member of the Ahl al-Bayt, was known for his knowledge of jurisprudence and hadith. He lived during the Abbasid Caliphate and is considered one of the major scholars of the Islamic Golden Age.
